Mechanism: PA's formate/succinate to CP carbon; CP's O2/serine/fumarate to PA respiration
Clinical_message: In the CSOM anaerobic environment, CP serves as an O2 and amino acid donor while PA recycles fermentation byproducts -- a true syntrophy. Single-target therapy may be insufficient.

Mechanism: SA's NH4 to CP amino acid synthesis; CP's serine to SA
Clinical_message: SA-CP co-infection is sustained by nitrogen cycling -- SA NH4 secretion fuels CP amino acid synthesis. Worth considering fungal identification even when only SA is cultured.

Mechanism: PA exploits OE's O2; CP forced to donate fumarate/serine/O2 at biosynthetic cost
Clinical_message: PA thrives in the OE aerobic environment even solo, while CP is suppressed by donating carbon, oxygen, and amino acids. Explains the clinical PA-dominance in OE through metabolic parasitism (PA exploits CP-derived substrates while suppressing CP growth). PA-targeted therapy is priority.

Mechanism: dcyt <-> deoxyuridine exchange -- DNA precursor swap reduces de novo synthesis cost
Clinical_message: In the nutrient-limited OE environment, SA-CP exploit nucleoside salvage (DNA precursor exchange) as a cooperative axis. Saves ATP cost of de novo synthesis, enabling rapid growth of both -- a chronicity risk.
